note.question: When should an informed supplier guarantee a capital-constrained buyer's bank loan, and how can the guarantee credibly signal buyer quality without distorting operations?
note.overview: An informed supplier signals a buyer's hidden risk to a competitive bank through wholesale price and credit guarantee; the paper derives refined perfect Bayesian equilibria.

components.label: Refined perfect Bayesian signaling equilibrium
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Refined perfect Bayesian signaling equilibrium. Proposition 2, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 9), gives the unique refined pooling equilibrium with wholesale price alone. Proposition 3, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 10), gives the unique refined separating equilibrium with wholesale price and guarantee, using Pareto dominance and the intuitive criterion.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The supplier observes buyer type and offers wholesale price and guarantee. The bank observes the contract, updates beliefs, and quotes a break-even interest schedule. The buyer chooses order quantity and borrows; production then succeeds or fails, determining repayment and guarantee liability. Wholesale price controls operational quantity.
